title_en.text: Agoo Basilica (Basilica Minore of Our Lady of Charity)

tagline.text: A Marian shrine on the La Union coast road, with a parish founded in 1578

location.label: Location
location.text: Along the national highway, Consolacion (Poblacion), Agoo, La Union

best_season.label: Best time to visit
best_season.text: November–May dry season (May 4 parish feast, Holy Week pilgrimage)

duration.label: Time needed
duration.text: 1–2 hours (half a day combined with San Fernando)

budget.label: Budget
budget.text: About ₱300~1,000 (per person, day trip; excludes round-trip transport from Manila; estimate includes offerings and snacks)

airport.label: Nearest airport
airport.text: Clark International Airport (CRK) or Ninoy Aquino International Airport (MNL), then overland

children.text: Agoo Basilica is the shrine of Our Lady of Charity in Agoo, La Union, where the parish was founded in 1578. Raised to a minor basilica by Pope John Paul II in 1982, it welcomes pilgrims with a Mexican Baroque church, a parish museum beside it, and a small statue of the Virgin that locals call Apo Caridad.
Agoo is a coastal city in southern La Union, about
236km
north of Manila and about
33km

south of the provincial capital, San Fernando. The basilica stands right beside the national highway in the Consolacion district at the center of town, and even from a bus passing through northern Luzon you can spot its gray facade and two bell towers. Its formal name is the Minor Basilica and Diocesan Shrine of Our Lady of Charity. It used to be called Santa Monica Church, and the Santa Monica parish is still based here.
The story begins in

, when Franciscan friars founded the parish and built a first church of wood, bamboo and nipa. In 1598 the Augustinians are said to have made Saint Monica the town's patron saint. The church was later destroyed by earthquakes and rebuilt several times. It was badly damaged by the great earthquake of
, and reconstruction began the following year. The present building had its cornerstone laid on
September 8, 1975
and was consecrated on
December 8, 1978
, the day that marked 400 years since Christianity reached Agoo.
On
Pope John Paul II raised the shrine to a minor basilica, recorded as the sixth of the twelve churches in the Philippines to receive that status. Then the magnitude 7.7 Luzon earthquake of

caused heavy damage again, and the old bell tower, the only part left of the 1893 building, collapsed. The church was repaired and reopened, and in 2001 a new bell tower and the Pope John Paul II Plaza were dedicated.
The heart of devotion is a 17th-century wooden statue of the Virgin about
30cm

tall. It is said to have been venerated first in Bantay, Ilocos Sur, and brought to Agoo by an Augustinian parish priest; the people of Agoo call it Apo Caridad. The apostolic nuncio crowned the image on May 1, 1971, and according to Wikipedia, Pope Francis approved a pontifical canonical coronation in 2024, which the apostolic nuncio presided over on
December 6, 2024
. Building and faith have endured together here, so it is a good stop for understanding Philippine Catholic culture whatever your own beliefs.

The reinforced concrete church was designed by architect Ignacio Palma Bautista in the Mexican Baroque style. A rose-window stained-glass panel sits above the gray facade, making it a good spot for photos.

The left tower is a four-level hexagon, while the right one is a bell gable, so the two do not match. After the 1990 earthquake brought down the old tower, a new belfry was built, and it connects to the Pope John Paul II Plaza in the yard.

This 17th-century wooden statue has a head of baked clay finished with white powder. The Christ Child blesses with his right hand and holds a golden globe in his left. A canopy over the altar is held up by four twisted columns.

Eight carved wooden panels with floral designs and a large crucifix at the top center fill the wall behind the altar. A pipe organ stands in the choir loft, and two-tiered chandeliers made of Philippine mahogany hang over the central aisle.

Near the confessional is a stained-glass window showing Jesus crucified between the two thieves, and the confessional and ceiling share a matching design. Near the main door, beside statues of Saints Peter and Paul, Hebrew letters are carved as a shortened form of the Ten Commandments.

blocks.title: Old church stones and a wishing well

children.text: The grounds have stone blocks from the old church, a garden and an old wishing well. The interior mural "The Second Coming of Christ" is by the artist Rey Gimeno.

The museum is in Bishop Mariano Madriaga Hall on the left side of the church. On the ground floor you can see the 1815 Santa Monica bell, found in Bugallon, Pangasinan, in 1963. The second floor holds memorabilia of Archbishop Antonio Mabutas, a native of Agoo, and others. Ask the parish about opening hours.

blocks.title: Holy Week pilgrimage and the May 4 feast

children.text: The basilica is a well-known pilgrimage site during Holy Week. The parish feast honors Saint Monica on
May 4
, and the feast of Our Lady of Charity is also said to fall on the same day, so the town is busiest around then.
Start at the highway-side facade and take in the rose window and the two bell towers. You can park in front of the church or on nearby streets, but it gets crowded around Mass times, so arrive early.

Step inside and look over the mahogany chandeliers along the central aisle, the altar screen and the pipe organ in the choir loft. If you can get close to the statue of the Virgin, do so quietly so that you do not disturb people praying.
Go back out to the grounds to see the old church stones, the garden and the wishing well, then walk across Pope John Paul II Plaza.
Check whether the parish museum (Madriaga Hall) beside the church is open, and see the 1815 bell and the archbishops' memorabilia.
If the parish office is open, you can ask about pilgrim information or Mass times. The office is said to be open Tuesday to Sunday and closed on Mondays and holidays.
Avoid taking photos or moving around during Mass; it is easier to plan your visit before or after services.
Leave Manila heading north. The drive usually takes several hours, so set out early to allow for traffic.
Arrive in Agoo and look around the basilica. Pray for a moment in front of the statue of the Virgin, or simply stand quietly.
Have lunch in Agoo town or in San Fernando to the north. Many people look for seafood and Ilocano dishes.
Continue about
33km
north to see Ma-Cho Temple and the coastal area of San Fernando.
Watch the sunset at San Juan beach or head straight back to Manila.
Doing it all in one day means a lot of driving, so consider staying overnight in San Juan, famous for surfing, and heading back the next day.
It is about
236km

north from Manila to Agoo. Take a long-distance bus toward the Ilocos region and get off in La Union. If you tell the driver in advance that you want to get off at Agoo, he can often drop you on the highway near the basilica.
By car or rental car, you can use NLEX, SCTEX and TPLEX to reach the La Union coastal highway. Check toll fees and times for each section on a map app and in expressway advisories before you leave.
Bus routes, fares and departure times change by company and season, so confirm locally.
From Clark International Airport (CRK), heading north on TPLEX gets you to the La Union coast sooner than starting from Manila. Flights change by season, so check airline announcements.
It is about
33km
south from central San Fernando to Agoo. Take a southbound bus or jeepney and get off in Agoo town.
From Baguio, come down by Naguilian Road or similar and then travel north or south along the coastal highway. Kennon Road is often restricted or closed, so check road advisories.
Use a tricycle for short trips in town and around the basilica. Ask the driver for the fare before you get in, and negotiate.

La Union has a tropical monsoon climate, and the dry season runs from November to May. Clear days are best for pilgrimage and photography, and the cooler months of December to February are ideal if you plan to spend longer walking the open grounds and plaza.

The busiest events are the May 4 parish feast and Holy Week. Masses and crowds make it hard to look around, and traffic and parking are congested, so choose a weekday morning if you want a quiet visit.

Near the basilica in Agoo town there are only simple eateries and shops, and not many places to stay. If you plan to stay overnight, there are more lodgings in San Fernando and San Juan to the north, so it is common to treat Agoo as a stop along the way.

In La Union and the Ilocos region you can try Ilocano food. On the way down from Baguio, many people look for vegetable dishes and grilled meat, and along the coast, fresh grilled seafood. It is uncertain whether any particular restaurant has been operating for long, so check ratings and opening status locally.

According to the parish listing, Mass is held on weekdays at 6 AM (Ilocano) and around 5:15 PM (English), and on Sundays several times from 5:30 AM to 4:30 PM. Times can change, so call the parish at (072) 710-0458 before you visit.
The parish office is said to be open Tuesday to Sunday from 9 AM to 12 noon and 2 to 5 PM, and closed on Mondays and holidays. Aim for these hours if you want to ask for the museum to be opened.
Dress modestly, covering the shoulders and knees. Avoid sleeveless tops and short pants.
During Mass, refrain from taking photos and speaking loudly, and do not walk in front of the altar.
On the May 4 feast day and during Holy Week, arrive early or come by public transport. It is safest to assume there is almost no parking.
Combining the visit with Ma-Cho Temple in San Fernando and San Juan beach makes for a full day.
Keep your belongings in front of you. Watch for pickpockets on days when pilgrims crowd the area.
This is a place of worship where the faithful pray, before it is a tourist attraction. During Mass and events, follow the instructions and look around quietly.
Mass schedules, museum hours and office closures can change with parish circumstances, so confirm by the official Facebook page and by phone.
Expect road congestion, a shortage of parking and large crowds during Holy Week and on May 4.
In La Union, typhoons and heavy rain can disrupt traffic on the coastal highway. Check the weather forecast during the rainy season.
Pilgrims gather here, so beware of pickpockets and overcharging, and do not leave bags unattended.
When photographing the statue of the Virgin and the altar decoration, do not disturb worshippers' prayers and do not use flash.
The provincial capital of La Union, about
33km
to the north, has Ma-Cho Temple, historic sites and a coastline. Many people visit it on the same trip.
A beach town famous for surfing, with plenty of lodging and cafes, good for an overnight stay.
A waterfall in inland La Union that makes a candidate when you want a change from the sea. Access and weather need to be confirmed locally.

blocks.title: Church of Saints Peter and Paul, Bauang

children.text: Another old church in La Union, which one blog presents as a neighboring stop to Agoo Basilica. Confirm the route and opening hours locally.
